# Headline

The slide headline: WPP Light at 54px, sentence case, two lines at most, at x = `m-edge` and y = `headline-y` (73px), with the orange eyebrow line beneath it at y = `eyebrow-y` (177px).

Three tiers ship. `headline` at 54px is the default. `headline-lg` at 64px is the size measured off the bank's own decks (32pt × 2) and is what the traced layouts use; the 54px default survives from an older point conversion and has not been re-decided. `headline-caps` at 48px is the ALL-CAPS "strong emphasis" variant, used on at most one content slide in four.

## The one highlight

A headline may carry exactly one highlight: the same size and colour, one weight up (Medium). Weight only: never orange, never underlined, never a size bump, and never inside body copy. Two highlights cancel each other out. Highlight only what the content owner marked; never invent one.

## The eyebrow

The line under the headline is Medium ALL CAPS at 24px, +0.12em, in `orange-800`, one of the sanctioned orange text moments. Keep it to a few words. Drop it when the headline runs to two lines: the second line crowds it.

## What the consumer supplies

The headline text, two lines at most (a third line is a content problem, not a type problem), and optionally the eyebrow, which only a one-line headline carries.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<h2 style="position:absolute; left:40px; top:73px; width:1840px; font-family:'WPP Light', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:54px; line-height:0.9; letter-spacing:-0.005em; color:#000050">Three moves that change the work</h2>
<p style="position:absolute; left:40px; top:177px; width:1840px; font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; letter-spacing:0.12em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#D94E0E">Operating principles</p>
```

For `headline-lg` set `font-size:64px`; for `headline-caps` set `font-size:48px; line-height:0.94; letter-spacing:0.01em; text-transform:uppercase`. On a navy slide the headline takes `color:#FFFFFF`. A layout that measures its headline elsewhere (some traced layouts set it at `m-text`, 56px, and lower) wins over these defaults: copy its preview. Beside a right-hand panel 768px or wider, the headline stops at 1040px.

Slides cannot change typeface inside a line, so the highlight cannot switch to `WPP Medium` mid-sentence. A headline that stays on one line with room to spare can keep it: at most 60 characters, spaces included, at 54px, 50 at 64px and 55 in capitals at 48px. Set it as a flex row of two or three `<h2>` blocks, the highlighted word alone in `'WPP Medium'`, and set the row's `gap` to the width of one word space: 15px at 54px, 18px at 64px, 14px in capitals at 48px.

```html
<div style="position:absolute; left:40px; top:73px; width:1840px; display:flex; flex-direction:row; align-items:baseline; gap:15px">
  <h2 style="font-family:'WPP Light', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:54px; line-height:0.9; letter-spacing:-0.005em; color:#000050">Three checks keep the copy</h2>
  <h2 style="font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:54px; line-height:0.9; letter-spacing:-0.005em; color:#000050">honest</h2>
</div>
```

A flex row cannot carry a headline onto a second line, so a longer headline stays one `<h2>` and drops the highlight. So does a split headline that an edit takes past its limit: set it back as one `<h2>`, without the highlight. Never fake the highlight with `<b>`, which synthesises a bold the system does not have.

## In the HTML deck

`.headline`, `.headline--lg` and `.headline--caps`, with `<span class="hl">` for the highlight and `.subtitle` for the eyebrow.

# Subhead

The Regular ALL-CAPS sub-headline at 24px, +0.08em, at the top of the content band. In the playbook's words it supports the headline, or leads the body copy.

This tier exists so that emphasis inside running text never needs bold. Every text tier differs from its neighbour by **weight or case, not just size**: Thin display, Light headline, Regular-caps subhead, Regular body, Medium-caps label. Bold ships only for the footer brand line.

## What the consumer supplies

One line, occasionally two. It sits above the body copy inside the content band, 20px above it.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<div style="position:absolute; left:40px; right:40px; top:305px; bottom:60px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:20px">
  <p style="max-width:1200px; font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; line-height:1.15; letter-spacing:0.08em; text-transform:uppercase">What changes for the client</p>
  <p style="max-width:1200px; font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:26px; line-height:1.32">Body copy follows the subhead.</p>
</div>
```

The outer `div` is the content band, from `band-top` (305px) to `band-bottom` (60px). It is pinned because 305px is deeper than a slide's padding can go.

## In the HTML deck

`.subhead`, inside `.content-band`.

# BodyCopy

Body copy is WPP Regular, three sizes by container: 26px in the content band, 24px in columns, 22px in four-column and box layouts. Line height 1.32, measure capped at 1200px.

## The floors

| Text | Floor |
|---|---|
| Body copy, and any text not in a fine-print role: paragraphs, bullets, column text | **20px** |
| Fine print: labels, chips, chart and table labels, each in one of the roles below | **16px** |
| Footer furniture only: page number, confidential line, source, brand line | **11px**, frozen |

These floors are this system's rule, and they replace Slides' own suggestion of 24px everywhere. If copy does not fit at its floor, the slide has too much content: split it or cut it. Never shrink type to fit.

## Fine print

Between 16 and 20px sits a closed list of roles, and nothing else. Running text never goes under 20px, and nothing but the footer furniture goes under 16px. A new role is a design decision made on this card, never a way to fit more copy.

| Role | What it is | In the HTML deck |
|---|---|---|
| Column label | the ALL-CAPS label over a column, a cell or a box | `col-sub` |
| Pill | the text inside a Pill | `pill` |
| Card link | a card's call to action | `card-cta` |
| Table header | a DataTable's header row | `datatable` |
| Stat label | the label under a stat circle, a KPI or a hero figure | `l` |
| Ramp label | the label on each step of an intensity ramp | `ramp-l1`, `ramp-l2`, `ramp-l3`, `ramp-l4` |
| Timeline label | a date or phase on a timeline's axis | `tl-label` |
| Milestone note | the short line under a milestone's label | `mb` |
| Fine label | a step, ruler, milestone or flag label, or the label over a run of sub-items | `fine-label` |
| Sub-item | a second-level entry under a heading | `sub-item` |
| Bio | a person's short bio | `bio` |
| Logo category | the category over a group of logos or items | `logo-cat` |
| Cell label | a label inside a matrix cell | `cell-label` |
| Taxonomy leaf | an entry at a taxonomy's last level | `tax-leaf` |
| Band label | the label of a band in a stack | `band-label` |

In the HTML deck an element takes its role's class beside its own, as in `class="fine-label step-l"`, and the verifier fails any text between 16 and 20px that carries none of them.

## No bold, no italics

There is no italic in the package, and bold emphasis inside body copy is banned outright. Emphasis inside running text is the Regular-caps Subhead tier or a Medium ALL-CAPS label, never a bold run.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<p style="max-width:1200px; font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:26px; line-height:1.32; color:#000050">Body copy in the content band.</p>
```

In columns use `font-size:24px`; in four-column and box layouts, `font-size:22px`. Never put `<b>` or `<i>` inside it.

## In the HTML deck

`.body`; `.cols .body` and `.cols-4 .body` step it down.

# ColumnLabel

The head of a column: a 16px Navy dot, then a Medium ALL-CAPS label at 24px (+0.12em), then the column's body copy. The dot sits 22px above the label, and the label 18px above the body.

Labels are Navy, never orange. Inside box layouts the label steps down to 20px. In icon-led columns a suite icon replaces the dot, when the point is a verb or a capability; never mix dots and icons on one slide.

## What the consumer supplies

A label of one to three words (the layouts' capacity puts most at 4–47 characters) and the column's copy.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:22px">
  <div style="width:16px; height:16px; border-radius:50%; background:#000050"></div>
  <div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:18px">
    <h3 style="font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; letter-spacing:0.12em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#000050">Automate</h3>
    <p style="font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; line-height:1.32">The shell, furniture and fixed slides come from the builder.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

In a box layout set the label to `font-size:20px`. Columns sit side by side in a flex row or grid; the layout sets their width and gutter.

## In the HTML deck

`.col-dot` and `.col-sub` (`.tbx .col-sub` in boxes).

# Pill

A fully rounded chip: `radius-pill`, padding 10 × 26px, flat Navy fill, White Medium ALL-CAPS label at 16px, +0.08em. On navy slides it inverts to a Cream fill with Navy text.

Rounding is reserved for pills. Cards, boxes, panels and tiles are square: flat fill, no border, no shadow, no rounded corners.

## What the consumer supplies

A short label: column headers, tags, category chips. 16px is the informational floor, so the label never goes smaller.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<p style="align-self:flex-start; background:#000050; color:#FFFFFF; border-radius:999px; padding:10px 26px; font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:16px; letter-spacing:0.08em; text-transform:uppercase">Strategy</p>
```

On a navy slide use `background:#FAFAF0; color:#000050`. `align-self:flex-start` keeps a pill in a column from stretching to the column's width. Several pills sit in a flex row; the layout sets the gap.

## In the HTML deck

`.pill`.

# DotBullet

The minor shape vocabulary, all of it flat Navy.

| Shape | Spec | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Dot bullet | Solid circle, Ø 16px, Navy or Orange 700 | Bullet marker, step separator between text boxes |
| Arrow | Solid Navy triangle, about 22 × 30px | Between process text boxes, carrying flow direction |
| Thin rule | 1px Navy line | Table row separators and timeline axes **only**, never a decorative underline |
| Left bracket | Thin Navy `[` | Grouping rows in tables and timelines |

There are no accent bars, no decorative rules and no underlines anywhere in the system. If no icon from the 32-icon suite fits a point, fall back to the dot bullet: it is always safe.

## In Claude Design Slides

A dot bullet beside 26px body copy; the 9px pad centres the dot on the first line, and the gap is illustrative:

```html
<div style="display:flex; flex-direction:row; gap:20px; align-items:flex-start">
  <div style="padding-top:9px"><div style="width:16px; height:16px; border-radius:50%; background:#000050"></div></div>
  <p style="font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:26px; line-height:1.32">One point, in body copy.</p>
</div>
```

The arrow between two text boxes, and the thin rule:

```html
<svg aria-label="then" width="22" height="30" viewBox="0 0 22 30"><path d="M0 0L22 15L0 30Z" fill="#000050"/></svg>
<hr style="width:1840px; border-top:1px solid #000050">
```

Draw the arrow as SVG: the stylesheet's border triangle needs wider borders than Slides allows, and Slides' own block-arrow shape is a different glyph.

## In the HTML deck

`.col-dot` for the column-header dot and `.sep-arrow` for the arrow.

# Takeaway

The closing line many layouts end on: one sentence in WPP Light at 48px, line height 1.15, held between two thin Navy corner brackets. It sits 160px in from each side and 120px above the bottom edge.

The brackets are 23px wide, drawn in a 1px Navy line (Cream on a navy slide), and open towards the text. They are one of two bracket devices, with the DotBullet card's left bracket for tables and timelines: never a box, never an underline, never orange. In split layouts, move the takeaway's right edge, never its left.

## What the consumer supplies

One sentence that says what the slide means, not a summary of it. Keep it to one line where possible, two at most.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<div style="position:absolute; left:160px; right:160px; bottom:120px; display:flex; flex-direction:row; align-items:stretch">
  <div style="width:23px; border-top:1px solid #000050; border-bottom:1px solid #000050; border-left:1px solid #000050"></div>
  <p style="flex:1; padding:14px 21px; font-family:'WPP Light', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:48px; line-height:1.15; color:#000050">Chosen layouts, not invented ones, is the whole trick.</p>
  <div style="width:23px; border-top:1px solid #000050; border-bottom:1px solid #000050; border-right:1px solid #000050"></div>
</div>
```

The brackets are two thin boxes either side of the text, stretched to its height; the 21px padding plus the 23px bracket makes the stylesheet's 44px inset. On a navy slide set the three strokes to `#FAFAF0` and the text to `#FFFFFF`.

## In the HTML deck

`.takeaway`, which draws the brackets as pseudo-elements.

# CardBox

Rectangles with **square corners, flat fill, no border and no shadow**. Fills come from White, Cream, Orange 500 and Navy only. Rounding belongs to pills; nothing else in the system is rounded.

The keyline on the fourth card in the preview only shows its edge; it is not part of the system. Cream-on-cream grouping is done by position and whitespace, not by drawing a box.

## Why there are no shadows

The system is flat by rule: no gradients, no drop shadows, no decorative rules, no accent bars. The drama comes from scale contrast (huge thin type against macro dots), not from ornament. The shipped stylesheet contains no `box-shadow` at all, which is the fastest way to check whether a deck has drifted off-brand.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<div style="background:#FFFFFF; padding:36px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px">
  <h3 style="font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:22px; color:#000050">White card</h3>
  <p style="font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:20px; line-height:1.32">Flat fill, square corners, no border, no shadow.</p>
</div>
```

Fills: `#FFFFFF`, `#FAFAF0`, `#FFF5CD` (Orange 500), or `#000050` with `color:#FFFFFF`. Never add `border`, `border-radius` or `box-shadow`. Leave the height out so the card grows with its text.

## In the HTML deck

`.card` (padding 36px) and the layouts' `.cell`, tint and navy panels.

# CardLink

The call to action at the foot of a card: WPP Medium at 18px in Navy, a word or two and an arrow ("More →"), pinned to the card's foot so the links line up across a row, at least 22px below the card's copy.

In the HTML deck the card is clickable: the link turns Orange 700 on hover and opens the card's hidden detail. That behaviour exists only in the HTML deck, and anything clickable there uses this one card pattern, never a hover of its own.

## What the consumer supplies

A short action ("More", "See the plan") and, in the HTML deck, the detail the card opens.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<div style="background:#FFFFFF; padding:36px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:space-between; gap:22px">
  <div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:22px">
    <h3 style="font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; letter-spacing:0.12em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#000050">Shell builder</h3>
    <p style="font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:22px; line-height:1.32">Generates the fixed slides from one spec.</p>
  </div>
  <p style="font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:18px; color:#000050">More →</p>
</div>
```

In a row, the cards stretch to one height and `justify-content:space-between` holds each link at its card's foot. A slide cannot expand a card, so in Slides the link is a label only: put the detail on the next slide or in the speaker notes, or leave the link out. It stays Navy; there is no hover.

## In the HTML deck

`.card-cta`, with `.arrow` for the arrow and `.card-detail` for what it opens.

# StatCircle

Every chart and diagram in this system is built from circles with flat fills from the primary and secondary palettes. No gradients, no 3-D, no outlines. A stat circle carries a Thin numeral at 90px with a Medium ALL-CAPS label at 18px beneath it.

## Size by area, not diameter

A circle twice the value is **√2 wider**, not twice as wide. Sizing by diameter quadruples the apparent magnitude and is the data-honesty failure the guideline calls out by name.

## Colour encodes intensity, never good or bad

The warm intensity ramp steps Orange 500 → 600 → 700 → 800/900 alongside the size step, for increasing magnitude or sequence. Text inside follows the accessibility matrix: Navy on light circles, White on Navy and Orange 900. There is no green and no red anywhere in the palette; direction is carried by the `+`/`−` sign and, where it is genuinely meaningful, by the single `data-pos` highlight.

## Stat anatomy

Numeral in Thin or Light at 90–150px Navy, the sign at full numeral size, and `%` set small and superscripted at roughly 25–30% of the numeral height. Label in Medium ALL CAPS 18px below.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<div style="width:300px; height:300px; border-radius:50%; background:#000050; color:#FFFFFF; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:10px">
  <p style="font-family:'WPP Thin', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:90px; line-height:1; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums">64%</p>
  <p style="max-width:240px; text-align:center; font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:18px; letter-spacing:0.1em; text-transform:uppercase">Segment one</p>
</div>
```

Size by area: against a reference circle of diameter D at value V, a value v gets the diameter D × √(v ÷ V), so 36% beside 64% at 300px is 225px. Numerals scale with the circle (68px at 225px and 46px at 150px in the preview), and labels in small circles go to the 16px floor. Orange 700 circles take `background:#FF7800; color:#000050`; Orange 600 circles take `background:#F9BD5D` with Navy text. Slides cannot size part of a line, so a small `%` needs its own text block beside the numeral, or stays at numeral size.

## In the HTML deck

`.stat-circle` and `.stat-circle--orange`, with `.v` and `.l`.

# KpiRow

A row of big stats, each above a short description: Thin numerals at 110px with tabular figures, the label beneath in Medium ALL CAPS at 18px, +0.1em. Above the row at its usual top of 340px a lead paragraph runs to one line; the five-step process row (ProcessTimelineV1) leaves no room for one. Donut percentages are drawn as filled circles, never as ring gauges.

## Direction semantics

When a number's direction is meaningful, give the room the cue. A favourable number takes `data-pos` (Orange 700); an unfavourable one takes `data-neg` (Navy), identical to default ink but chosen on purpose.

**Favourable follows meaning, not sign.** "−41% cycle time" glows; "+8% churn" does not. Neutral figures such as market sizes, headcounts and dates stay in the composition's default colour. The content owner decides direction; never guess it from the arithmetic sign.

**One glowing number per slide, maximum.** If everything glows, nothing does.

## The contrast catch

Orange 700 thin numerals on Cream measure about 2.5:1. A favourable numeral therefore goes up to Light (never Thin) below 90px, or sits on White. At 90px and up, Thin is fine as wayfinding-scale type. The middle numeral in the preview is set in Light for exactly this reason.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<div style="position:absolute; left:40px; right:80px; top:340px; display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3, 1fr); gap:80px">
  <div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px">
    <p style="font-family:'WPP Thin', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:110px; line-height:1; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums">$2M</p>
    <p style="font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:18px; line-height:1.2; letter-spacing:0.1em; text-transform:uppercase">Annual run-rate saving</p>
  </div>
  <div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px">
    <p style="font-family:'WPP Light', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:110px; line-height:1; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; color:#FF7800">−41%</p>
    <p style="font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:18px; line-height:1.2; letter-spacing:0.1em; text-transform:uppercase">Onboarding cycle time</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

One column per stat: `repeat(N, 1fr)`. The low variant sits the row 150px from the bottom instead of at `top:340px`.

## In the HTML deck

`.kpi-row` (and `.kpi-row--low`), `.kpi` with `.v`, and `.stat--pos` / `.stat--neg` for direction.

# DataTable

Tables are hairlines and type, nothing else. Headers are Medium ALL CAPS at 16px (+0.1em) over a 1px Navy rule; cells are Regular at 22px with a 1px Navy rule beneath each row; padding is 14px vertical, 48px to the right.

No fills, no zebra striping, no vertical rules, no borders around the table. The 1px Navy line is sanctioned for table row separators and timeline axes **only**; it is never a decorative underline.

## What the consumer supplies

The data. Keep cells short: table cells are informational text under the 16px floor, so a table that needs smaller type needs fewer columns instead.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<table style="font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-size:22px; color:#000050">
  <tr><th style="width:40%; font-weight:400">WORKSTREAM</th><th style="width:30%; font-weight:400">OWNER</th><th style="width:30%; font-weight:400">STATUS</th></tr>
  <tr><td>Data foundations</td><td>Client data team</td><td>In build</td></tr>
</table>
```

Slides sets one typeface and size per table and cannot letter-space a header cell, so headers stay in the table's face: write them in capitals and keep them short. Slides rules the rows itself; add no row fills. Every cell of the first row needs its `width:N%`.

## In the HTML deck

`.datatable`.

# LogoRow

One row of a categorised logo wall: the category as a Medium ALL-CAPS label at 24px, held at least 200px wide, then the logos 40px apart, each at most 44px tall and 110px wide. Rows are 16px tall above and below, with a hairline in Navy at 10% opacity between them and none under the last.

Partner logos are supplied per deck; the system ships none. Partner co-branding follows the Logo guideline.

## What the consumer supplies

The category labels and each partner's logo file, uploaded into the deck.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<div style="display:flex; flex-direction:row; align-items:center; gap:40px; padding:16px 0px; border-bottom:1px solid rgba(0,0,80,0.1)">
  <p style="min-width:200px; flex-shrink:0; font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:24px; letter-spacing:0.12em; text-transform:uppercase; color:#000050">Cloud</p>
  <img src="/_blob/<id>" alt="[Partner name]" style="width:110px; height:44px; object-fit:contain">
</div>
```

Stack the rows in a flex column; leave the border off the last row. Every logo gets the same 110 × 44px box with `object-fit:contain`, so marks of different shapes line up.

## In the HTML deck

`.logo-row`, with `.col-sub` as its label.

# ScreenshotFrame

The sanctioned way to show a screenshot: the image at its own proportions with a 1px Navy keyline, and nothing else. No shadow, no device frame, no rounded corners, no tilt, and never full-bleed.

## What the consumer supplies

The screenshot, uploaded into the deck, and a caption or callouts from the layout that hosts it.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<img src="/_blob/<id>" alt="[What the screenshot shows]" style="width:960px; height:600px; object-fit:contain; border:1px solid #000050">
```

Size the box to the screenshot's own proportions so the keyline hugs the image; `object-fit:contain` keeps every pixel visible. When the screenshot has to be explained, use the MediaAnnotatedCallouts4 layout.

## In the HTML deck

`.screenshot`.

# Photo

A photograph in the system's navy duotone, navy in its shadows and white in its highlights, cropped to its box. Guideline 08 says when a photo is used and which renderings are allowed; this card says how to set one.

## Which photos take the duotone

- **A photo the brief supplies**, in colour or not, takes it.
- **The thirteen photos in the Photography group are already navy duotone.** Place them as they are, and never put them through the duotone a second time.

## Placing it

A photo 200 × 200px or larger that stands alone on the slide touches a canvas edge: it bleeds off an edge or sits in a corner. Inside a card, a tile or a portrait, or as one of a row of three or more photos of the same size, it sits where the layout puts it.

A full-bleed duotone photo is a poster moment for high-impact decks only; otherwise a photo takes half the slide or a panel.

## What the consumer supplies

The photo, copied into the deck, and a short alt text that says what it shows.

## In Claude Design Slides

A photo the brief supplies, filling the right half of the slide:

```html
<div style="position:absolute; right:0px; top:0px; width:960px; height:1080px; overflow:hidden; background:#000050">
  <img src="/_blob/<id>" alt="[What the photo shows]" style="width:960px; height:1080px; object-fit:cover; filter:grayscale(1) contrast(1.08) brightness(1.04); mix-blend-mode:screen">
</div>
```

Size the Navy box as the layout's preview sizes its media area, and give the image the same width and height. A photo from the Photography group is a plain `<img>` with `object-fit:cover`, without the Navy box and the filter.

## In the HTML deck

`.duo` around the image, placed by the layout; a library photo is placed with `data-motif` and never wrapped in `.duo`.

# Icon

Brand icons are built from dots: the glyph outline is drawn as a string of solid circles of varying diameter, with a loose scatter of tiny satellite dots around it. One colour per icon, never multicolour. Icons are 44px Navy by default and 64px in the large host, with one sanctioned orange moment, and they turn Cream on navy slides and panels. The squares in the preview stand in for the glyphs; the 32 real icons are in the **Icons** asset group.

## The pairing rule is hard

**One weight family per icon row, per slide.** A monoline icon beside a solid one in the same row reads as two different icon sets, the most visible amateur tell in the whole system. The deck-wide default is **solid**; use **line** only when every icon on the slide is line, and **bold** only in hosts of 44px or more. Where both styles of a glyph exist (`flow` / `workflow`), the family decides for you.

## When not to use one

Icon-led columns replace dot headers **when the point is a verb or a capability**; dot headers stay the default for parallel nouns. Never mix both header styles on one slide. Never substitute a generic icon library: if no suite icon fits, fall back to the dot bullet.

`spark` and `spark-bold` are accents, not bullets: two per deck at most, in statement-adjacent air only.

## In Claude Design Slides

Paste the icon's SVG from the Icons group inline, give it an `aria-label`, size it to 44 × 44px (64 × 64px for the large host), and set its ink by replacing every `currentColor` with a hex value: `#000050` by default, `#FAFAF0` on navy slides and panels, `#FF7800` for the one orange moment. As an `<img>` the file's `currentColor` has nothing to inherit and renders black. Every icon file is well under Slides' 52 KB limit for inline SVG. Never use Slides' own `x-icon` set: it is a generic library.

## In the HTML deck

`<div class="icon"><svg …></svg></div>`, with `.icon--lg` and `.icon--orange`.

# DotField

*"The dot is the most important device in our storytelling."* Everything in the system (backgrounds, illustrations, icons, charts, bullets) is built from circles. When in doubt, express it with a dot. The default dot colour is Orange 700.

Three registers:

| Register | Diameter | Reads as |
|---|---|---|
| **Micro** | 1–1.5% of canvas width, about 20–30px | Dense organic scatter, irregular non-grid spacing, densest at the heart and dissolving outward. Stipple texture, energy. |
| **Mid** | 15–25% of width, about 290–480px | A dozen circles drifting across a zone, several overlapping or fused into peanut shapes, several cropped by the edges. |
| **Macro** | 60–110% of width | Three or four enormous circles, **always heavily cropped** by the canvas edges so they read as crops, never as balls. |

**Fused metaballs are sanctioned.** Two same-colour circles overlapping merge into one flat peanut silhouette. One or two fused pairs per composition is the house accent; ten is noise.

## Hard rules

- Never a single circular shape carrying more visual weight than the canvas. Dots appear as a composition, or bleed off the edge as a crop, never as one dominating centred ball.
- **One hue per register field.** The corner and edge accent presets (`field-right`, `field-bottom`, `field-tl`, `field-accent`) mix up to three sanctioned colours; the agenda and the classic divider carry multi-colour scatters.
- Flat fill, no transparency, no strokes. Same-colour circles may overlap and merge.
- Only the sanctioned background × dot pairings, listed in the Colour guideline.
- **Navy dots never sit behind text.** The one exception is a divider title in White knocked out of a large navy dot.
- Dots anchor to edges and corners; the content zone stays clear.
- Tone-on-tone (white on cream, cream on white) is the subtlest treatment and is always safe.
- Corner dots may run under the footer; they stay White or Cream so the footer still reads.

The micro field in the preview is generated from a fixed seed so the card is stable.

## In Claude Design Slides

Draw the whole field as one `<svg>` pinned full-bleed and listed first on the slide, so later content paints over it and cropped circles clip at the canvas edge. Separate pinned circles cannot do this, because Slides clamps negative offsets to 0.

```html
<svg aria-label="" width="1920" height="1080" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" style="position:absolute; left:0px; top:0px; width:1920px; height:1080px">
  <circle cx="1920" cy="80" r="280" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <circle cx="1890" cy="590" r="150" fill="#FFF5CD"/>
  <circle cx="1923" cy="385" r="75" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
  <circle cx="1825" cy="835" r="45" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
</svg>
```

That is the `field-right` preset the kit layouts use. The presets in the layout previews list each dot as diameter, left, top and colour key: the circle's centre is at left + d/2, top + d/2, and its radius is d/2. A fused pair is two same-colour circles that overlap.

### The mid and macro fields

The two register fields in their shipped colours, Orange 600 for the mid field and Orange 500 for the macro.

The `field-mid` preset:

```html
<svg aria-label="" width="1920" height="1080" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" style="position:absolute; left:0px; top:0px; width:1920px; height:1080px">
  <circle cx="1910" cy="50" r="210" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
  <circle cx="1500" cy="50" r="170" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
  <circle cx="2000" cy="540" r="240" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
  <circle cx="1570" cy="410" r="150" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
  <circle cx="1700" cy="740" r="180" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
  <circle cx="1850" cy="830" r="130" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
  <circle cx="1210" cy="870" r="150" fill="#F9BD5D"/>
```

## In the HTML deck

The `data-dots` presets (`field-right`, `field-bottom`, `field-tl` and others), drawn by a small script in each layout preview.

# FooterFurniture

Standing furniture on every content slide, divider and outro. Four elements, all at frozen sizes:

| Element | Set | Position |
|---|---|---|
| Brand line | Bold 700, 16px, +0.01em | right `m-edge`, bottom 34px |
| Page number | Regular 400, 11px caps, 70% opacity, written `04 / 13` | right `m-edge`, bottom 14px |
| Confidential line | Regular 400, 11px caps, 70% opacity, `PRIVATE & CONFIDENTIAL` | left `m-edge`, bottom 14px |
| Source | Regular 400, 12px, 75% opacity | left `m-edge`, bottom 60px |

On a navy slide the brand line and page number flip to White. The source line appears only when a claim is cited. The confidential line is set per deck: when the deck is confidential it goes on every slide except the cover. The cover has the logo badge instead of a footer strip; dividers and the outro keep the strip.

## The name

The lockup reads **`WPP Enterprise Solutions | MAP`**, the organisation's full name and the only one used in decks. Never "VML MAP", never "VMLMAP". In running prose, write it in full on first mention and "MAP" thereafter.

## The 11px floor is frozen

11px is for furniture only, and closed. No new text ever ships at that size; the informational floor for everything else is 16px.

## In Claude Design Slides

```html
<p style="position:absolute; right:40px; bottom:34px; width:800px; text-align:right; font-family:'WPP Medium', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:16px; letter-spacing:0.01em; color:#000050">WPP Enterprise Solutions | MAP</p>
<p style="position:absolute; right:40px; bottom:14px; width:200px; text-align:right; font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:11px; letter-spacing:0.08em; text-transform:uppercase; opacity:0.7; color:#000050">04 / 13</p>
<p style="position:absolute; left:40px; bottom:14px; width:800px; font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:11px; letter-spacing:0.08em; text-transform:uppercase; opacity:0.7; color:#000050">Private &amp; Confidential</p>
<p style="position:absolute; left:40px; bottom:60px; width:1200px; font-family:'WPP', sans-serif; font-weight:400; font-size:12px; opacity:0.75; color:#000050">Source: [source]</p>
```

In Slides the brand line is set in `WPP Medium`, not Bold: Bold would be a fifth face, and a deck loads four. These positions replace Slides' own 24px footer row. On a navy slide, set the brand line and page number to `#FFFFFF`. The HTML deck computes page numbers from the live slide count; in a Slides deck they are typed, so update them when slides are added, removed or moved.

## In the HTML deck

`.footer-brand`, `.pageno`, `.confidential` and `.source`.
